A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same affinity-score research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic activation-function measurements, ImageNet architecture analyses, CIFAR experiments and supervised/self-supervised model comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical analyses, revises architecture and accuracy comparisons, and adds numerical polynomial-function demonstrations.

M1.justification: The affine optimal-transport map, normalized Wasserstein affinity score, activation-level signature, spatial averaging and covariance shrinkage remain. The rewritten signature definition aligns its argument order with the input-to-output construction already described in v1; it does not establish a different computational procedure.

E1.justification: v2 Figure 2C extends the synthetic function examples beyond activation functions to polynomials of orders 1, 3, 7 and 41. ImageNet-1K, CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and random-input coverage remain; changes to the architecture pool occur within retained vision tasks.

E2.justification: The alternatives to affinity remain linear CKA, norm, sparsity, entropy and regression R². Depth, parameter count and operations were already evaluated as accuracy predictors in v1 Appendix I. The supervised/self-supervised comparison methods are also retained.

E3.justification: The main clustering/correlation pool changes membership, including MNASNet and EfficientNet entries in place of MaxViT, ShuffleNet and Wide-ResNet entries. Accuracy analysis changes from v1 Figure 20's four groups to five groups in v2 Figure 4, with revised signature statistics and explicit R² reporting; v1 already mentioned R² for fit selection. The 50,000-image ImageNet validation set and batch size 512 remain.

E4.justification: The polynomial-order sensitivity demonstration in v2 Figure 2C adds a bounded sanity check of the score. Existing batch-size, seed, depth, dataset-shift and residual-connection analyses largely survive. The residual ablation's new distribution plots mainly redisplay the earlier comparison rather than introduce another ablation.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix F reports ResNet20 accuracies as means and standard deviations over five seeds; v2 retains the residual comparison in Figure 5D but omits that run-count and uncertainty disclosure. The nine-seed VGG experiment, batchwise standard deviations and activation boxplot reporting remain. This does not establish a change in runs actually performed.

E6.justification: Central accuracy results are replaced under revised groupings and statistics: v1 reports traditional-model Max/Mean correlation 0.755, whereas v2 reports Max/Median R² values 0.512 for pre-residual and 0.814 for residual models. These are not like-for-like performance gains. v2 also adds detailed correlation tables and polynomial scores, while removing the ResNet20 accuracies 90.77±0.24 and 91.74±0.28 reported in v1.

T1.justification: v2 narrows the main-text Corollary 3.2 assumption from positive semidefinite to positive definite, although its appendix retains the earlier wording. Definition 3.1 corrects the affinity argument order, and new Remark 3.6 adds mathematical reasoning contrasting affinity with linear regression and R². The principal transport results and proofs otherwise remain.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies network non-linearity measurement as approximate and makes the pre-transformer linearization trend and transformer reversal central conclusions. The affinity-score proposal, architecture identification, performance associations and distinction from other metrics were already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: New Appendix B discusses the positive-definite assumption and acknowledges that optimizing affinity has not been shown to improve accuracy, robustness or transferability. v2 also links residual-score bimodality to identity learning and interprets the transformer transition as a change in implicit bias, extending the earlier architectural explanations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code repository link in the abstract and retains pooling, shrinkage and validation details, partly in Appendix E. However, it omits v1's explicit CIFAR10 attribution for the ResNet20 ablation and logarithmic-transformation description for complexity-predictor fits. The PDFs establish an added access statement, not independently verified code availability.

R1.justification: v2 substantially reframes the research gap around limitations of depth/width-based expressivity comparisons across architectures. It adds supporting expressivity literature, including Eldan and Shamir, Bartlett et al. and Vardi et al., plus transformer/LLM context, while removing works such as Hanin and Xiong et al. The direct OT, CKA and Philipp comparisons remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. The method explanation is reorganized around the non-linearity signature, the architecture-by-architecture narrative becomes a thematic synthesis, substantial material moves into reorganized appendices, and the conclusion becomes a broader discussion with new limitations and impact sections.

P2.justification: v2 adds the method illustration and function examples, introduces a historical summary chart, and redesigns architecture comparisons as a large clustering/distribution composite. Many raw-signature plots are consolidated or relocated, activation plots are merged, and correlation displays become summary and detailed tables. These changes substantially alter the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the method and cross-architecture findings easier to understand, adds code-access information and detailed correlation tables, and explicitly qualifies the practical implications in Appendix B. These gains are limited by lost ResNet20 seed/accuracy reporting and unexplained table discrepancies: EfficientNet CKA is 0.42 in Table 1, while Table 2's entries average about 0.37. With the core method and proofs largely retained, the net improvement is chiefly clarity and qualification.
